title: Singing through megaphones and owning the first amplifying set
summary: DeDroit recalls singers with megaphones, being the first local leader to own a public-address set, and Mobile and Hattiesburg dates, with side chatter.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What do you remember about singers singing to the megaphone? Do you remember much about that period?
Yes, yes, who used that? Sure. Who used to sing for you? Well, in Biloxi, George Potter, my banjo player,
was my son. And he sang to a megaphone. When did that go out? When did you start using microphones?

When I went out with the microphones. I was the first band leader in town to own an amplifying set. Amplifying set? Yeah. When would that be? I used to carry it around with two speakers. I mean, what year was that? Oh, I went through here. You see, I used to play a lot of cardboard balls in Mobile. And they write me a lot of fank. I mean, that's how I get the dates, because I don't remember dates. And I remember that I used it over there first. It was called
the quarter box. You want me to look through it and find Mobile for you? Well, I can do it. It'll help you.
I used to play a lot of people. I used to play the Hattiesburg Country Club. I used to play the Hattiesburg Country Club.

Oh, that was a not-willing job. I stayed in Admiral Simms for one of my honeymoons. You did? Was Frank Lane the manager? You did what? You think you did, anyway. I think I spent the night there. My honeymoon night, I spent that.

Sule College. Look at the president of Sule College. You see, this was in a fire. I had two washrooms windows when I lived on Cadiz Street, and we used one for the library, and the fire had to break out our face.
